action: Public bodies: block unknown USB devices, keep offline backups, keep systems updated and avoid suspicious links or attachments, as MP-CERT advises.
date_note: Published November 19; the article does not say when the attack happened.
exec: A police computer was encrypted by ransomware that arrived on a USB drive; it shows removable media can still be a way in for public bodies.
plain: A computer at a police station in Bhopal, India, was locked by ransomware that came in on a pen drive. The state's cyber team says it unlocked the files without paying and found no sign of data theft.
summary: Free Press Journal reports that a computer at Ayodhya Nagar police station in Bhopal was hit by ransomware introduced through a pen drive. Officials told the paper that MP-CERT decrypted and recovered the data without the attackers' help and found no evidence of leakage or theft. No actor or ransom demand is named.
title: Ransomware hits Bhopal police station computer; MP-CERT recovers data without paying

validation.note: One outlet (Free Press Journal, Nov 19) read in full; it relies on unnamed officials and an MP-CERT Joint Director.

review.note: Compared title, station and city, pen drive vector, MP-CERT recovery without attackers, no leakage or theft finding, Nov 19 publication date and no actor against the Free Press Journal article
